title: Diagnose an UPDATE_FAILED VCF Automation deployment from its request logs
prompt:
A production deployment in our VMware Cloud Foundation Automation 9.1 environment is sitting in UPDATE_FAILED and the on-call runbook still has a human clicking through the UI to work out why. Finish the client that does it automatically.

Everything is in this repository. `src/VcfaTriage.java` is a single-file Java client with one unimplemented method, `triage(String deploymentId)`. It is the only file you should change. `README.md` specifies the triage procedure, the remediation runbook and the exact nine-line report format `triage` must return. `docs/contract.json` is the API contract you code against, and `docs/official_sources.json` records where each operation in it came from.

Run `./run_tests.sh`. It compiles your client together with the harness, runs it against a loopback mock of the deployment API, and then grades both the report and the exact shape of the HTTP traffic your client produced. Nothing leaves 127.0.0.1 and there are no third-party dependencies — stock JDK and CPython only.

Two things the grader is strict about, both of which come straight from the contract:

- The failure cause is not in the deployment summary and not in any event's `details` string. Several of those actively point the wrong way. You have to page through the request's events, pull the failing event's logs, and read them. The runbook keys off the log evidence, not off the summary.
- Optional parameters and body fields that you have no value for are omitted from the wire entirely. Not an empty string, not `{}`, not `null`, and not a server default you did not actively choose.

Done means `./run_tests.sh` exits zero with every check passing.

verification.description: Starts the loopback mock on 127.0.0.1, compiles src/VcfaTriage.java with harness/TestMain.java and harness/Json.java, runs one triage, then verify/verify.py asserts the nine-line report and the recorded request wire shape. 45 checks; all must pass. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

reference_fix.description: Reference implementation of VcfaTriage.triage. Applying it to the shipped tree makes all 45 checks pass.

notes.contractProvenance: VCF Automation has no OpenAPI document in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository. docs/contract.json was transcribed by hand from the Broadcom xAPIs reference pages for the VM Apps Org - Catalog reference set; every page URL, the operation it documents and the date it was fetched are recorded in docs/official_sources.json. contract.json states this in its sourceStatement field.
notes.scenario: Deployment payments-api-prod is UPDATE_FAILED. Its lastRequest is a dismissed failure whose details blame a storage policy; the open failure is an older, non-dismissed request. That request's failing event sits on the second page of events, its details string says only 'Task failed', and the real cause — an active VM snapshot blocking disk reconfiguration — appears only in the second slice of that event's logs. The runbook maps that cause to the Delete Snapshot day-2 action, which takes no inputs, so the submitted ResourceActionRequest must carry actionId and reason and omit inputs.
notes.mock: mock/vcfa_mock.py binds an ephemeral port on 127.0.0.1 and serves only the seven operations docs/contract.json names; anything else is a 404. It requires the bearer token, rejects non-integer paging parameters, rejects unknown ResourceActionRequest fields, and appends every request to .run/requests.jsonl for the verifier to read.
notes.mutationTesting: The verifier was checked against 14 mutated clients: unimplemented stub, sending inputs:{}, sending sinceRow on the first log call, triaging the dismissed lastRequest, reading only the first event page, stopping after the first log slice, guessing the storage-policy remediation, submitting Resize, an ungrounded reason, a duplicate submission, submitting before reading the logs, probing actions for every resource, calling an operation outside the contract, and dropping the Accept header. Each was caught by its intended check.
